questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Push or pull?
questions.explanation: We push a ball when we kick it, push a door shut and push a trolley. We pull a kite string, pull a bucket rope and a tractor pulls a trailer.

questions.stem: Which one do we push?
questions.explanation: We push a trolley away from us. We pull a kite string and a bucket rope towards us.

questions.stem: Which one shows a pull?
questions.explanation: Pulling up a bucket on a rope is a pull. Kicking a ball and shutting a door are pushes.

questions.stem: A push moves something away from you.
questions.explanation: A push moves things away from us. A pull moves things towards us.

questions.stem: A pull moves something towards you.
questions.explanation: A pull brings things closer to us, like pulling a cart or a kite string.

questions.stem: Opening a drawer is a ___.
questions.explanation: We pull a drawer towards us to open it.

questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: Match what we do to what happens.
questions.explanation: Kicking a still ball starts it moving. Catching a rolling ball stops it. Pedalling harder makes a bicycle go faster.

questions.stem: Put the boat story in order.
questions.explanation: The boat comes back from the river. Then the people push and pull it. At the end it is up on the bank.

questions.stem: Which will roll down a slope?
questions.explanation: A ball is round, so it rolls down a slope. A flat book or a box slides but does not roll.

questions.stem: Mina wants her toy car to go faster. What can she do?
questions.explanation: A bigger push makes the car go faster. A small push makes it go slowly and holding it makes it stop.

questions.stem: A push from a friend makes Tuli's swing go faster.
questions.explanation: A push can make something go faster, like a swing.

questions.stem: Tap how the people move the heavy boat.
questions.explanation: The people pulled the rope and pushed the back of the boat. Sleeping and eating do not move a boat.

questions.subskill: Pushes and pulls in a simulation
questions.stem: The cart stays still when both teams pull the same.

sim.task: Open Forces and Motion: Basics and choose Net Force. Put one small puller on the blue rope on the left and one small puller on the red rope on the right. Press Go and watch the cart.

questions.explanation: When both sides pull with the same strength, the pulls cancel out and the cart does not move.

questions.subskill: Pushes and pulls in a simulation
questions.stem: Which way does the cart go?

sim.task: Open Forces and Motion: Basics and choose Net Force. Put one small puller on the blue rope on the left. Put two small pullers on the red rope on the right. Press Go and watch the cart.

questions.explanation: Two pullers pull harder than one puller. The cart goes to the red side where there are more pullers.

questions.stem: Which animal can pull a cart?
questions.explanation: A cow or a water buffalo is strong and can pull a cart. Fish and owls cannot.

questions.stem: Example: car 7 tiles, bus 4, rickshaw 5. Which went farthest?
questions.explanation: Compare the numbers. The red car rolled 7 tiles, which is more than 5 or 4.

questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: A ball starts to roll. A push or pull made it.
questions.explanation: Things do not start moving by themselves. A push or a pull makes them move.

questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: A push can make a ball do what?
questions.explanation: A push can make a ball roll, speed up, slow down or change direction. It cannot make a ball sing or grow.

questions.stem: Tap the things we push.
questions.explanation: We push a trolley and we push a ball when we kick it. We pull a kite string and a bucket rope.

questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: A push can make a moving thing stop.
questions.explanation: A push can stop something, like a hand stopping a rolling ball.
